empty.body: Load a model to start collecting live telemetry.

idle.title: No generation yet
idle.body: Statistics appear after the first run — buffer, speed and paging counters start at zero.

note.gpuBody: llama.cpp manages the weights inside its own process (GPU offload + its own mmap), so shard-buffer, prefetch-accuracy and RAM page-cache telemetry don't apply here. Generation speed, tokens, and (on Windows) paging demand below are real measurements; VRAM usage is reported live by llama-server.

gauge.hitRateTip: Shard reads served from the streaming buffer vs total accesses.
gauge.hitRateGpuTip: llama-server manages weights inside its own process — there is no shard-level buffer to measure.
gauge.hitRateCaveat: Real value — always 0% in practice: llama.cpp reads its own mmap, so the tracker never sees those reads (ADR-003). Use Paging Demand as the main signal.
gauge.hitRateGpuCaveat: GPU backend: weights live inside llama-server (GPU offload), so there is no shard buffer to track. The VRAM note above is the real residency signal.
gauge.residencyTip: Share of the model file held in the OS page cache.
gauge.speedTip: Tokens per second of the most recent generation on this model.
gauge.prefetchTip: Useful prefetches divided by all prefetches. n/a when no prefetch activity was measured.
gauge.pagingTip: Process-wide page faults per token during the last generation (dominated by the model mmap).
gauge.pagingNa: n/a · not measured by this backend

chart.window: session window · since opening this page

paging.title: Paging demand detail
paging.tip: From the last generation: process-wide soft+hard faults; disk demand is measured from major faults (POSIX) or estimated from model-file residency growth (Windows).
paging.idle: No generation yet — paging counters start after the first run.
paging.unavailable: Not measured on this platform (page cache tracking is Windows-only).
paging.unavailableGpu: Not measured — llama-server runs inference in its own process; page-fault sampling is attached on Windows only.

heatmap.title: MoE expert activity
heatmap.tip: Cells light up only from real telemetry. Stock llama.cpp does not expose per-token expert routing, so the grid stays dark — never animated with fake firing.
heatmap.notMoeBody: Dense model — there is no expert routing to display.
